paper_metadata.title: Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm for Portfolio Selection: A Comparative Study with Classical Markowitz Optimization

summary: The paper demonstrates QAOA for a small synthetic portfolio optimization instance with 6 assets (6 qubits) using Qiskit Aer and 1024 shots. QAOA achieves QUBO costs of −17.740 (p=1) and −17.630 (p=2), compared with the exact classical QUBO optimum of −17.745. The study explicitly reports no quantum advantage and frames the experiment as a pedagogical demonstration of mapping portfolio optimization to QAOA.

experiments.description: QAOA applied to a 6-asset discrete portfolio selection QUBO, evaluated at depths p=1 and p=2 on a Qiskit simulator and compared against an exact classical QUBO solver baseline.

algorithm.variant: standard QAOA for QUBO portfolio selection

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per binary asset-selection variable; xi in {0,1} indicates whether asset i is included
problem_formulation.objective_function: Cost(x) = - sum_i mu_i x_i + lambda * sum_{i,j} Sigma_ij x_i x_j + penalty terms
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: penalty terms for cardinality and portfolio-size/budget constraints
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_C = sum_i h_i Z_i + sum_{i<j} J_ij Z_i Z_j + constant

problem_instance.description: Small synthetic discrete portfolio selection instance

dataset_specification.description: synthetically generated expected returns and covariance matrix; no real market dataset used

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: synthetic generation of mu_i and Sigma_ij to create a controlled, reproducible small instance
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Single instance evaluated with QAOA at p=1 and p=2; results compared to exact classical QUBO optimum

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: synthetic generation of returns/covariance and QUBO construction
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: bitstring extraction and comparison of expected return, variance, and QUBO cost

speedup_claims.conditions: small 6-asset instance on a classical simulator; paper explicitly states no practical advantage over classical methods
speedup_claims.caveats: No quantum advantage is claimed; QAOA is presented as pedagogical/exploratory. p=2 performed slightly worse than p=1 due to non-convex optimization.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: not reported; experiment limited to n = 6 assets (6 qubits)
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not analyzed in the paper; scaling would require far more qubits and deeper circuits than available NISQ devices.
limiting_factors: experiment performed only on a classical simulator
very small problem size (6 qubits / 6 assets)
no asymptotic speedup or complexity advantage claimed
variational optimization instability (p=2 worse than p=1)
classical exact QUBO solver reaches slightly lower cost (-17.745 vs -17.740)

notes: circuit_depth not explicitly given as a total depth; inferred only that depths p=1 and p=2 were evaluated, so total circuit depth is left null and num_layers records the evaluated QAOA depths.
